faq.q: Why does this page stop at $500,000 — is that just an asking-price filter?
faq.a: It is a price filter, but the line also matches a federal financing tier: CMHC states homes $500,000 or less require a minimum 5% down payment, while homes between $500,000 and $1,499,999 require 5% on the first $500,000 plus 10% on any amount over $500,000.

faq.q: Are these Jared Gibbons' own listings?
faq.a: No. The visible cards are other brokerages' listings (Royal LePage - Wolstencroft and Stonehaus Realty Corp. on the cards read for this file), with Jared's contact block shown as the site owner on each card, not as the listing agent.

faq.q: Can a first-time buyer avoid property transfer tax on a condo on this page?
faq.a: On price alone, yes: the first time home buyers' program exempts a qualifying purchaser on the first $500,000 of the purchase price and its full exemption requires a fair market value of $835,000 or less — every home on this page is under that value threshold, though the program's other conditions still have to be met.

faq.q: What should I read before buying a condo in this area?
faq.a: The Form B, the bylaws, the last two years of strata minutes, the depreciation report and the contingency reserve fund balance. They show planned repairs, special levies and rules on pets and rentals.

faq.q: What do strata fees cover on a condo in this area?
faq.a: Strata fees pay for upkeep and insurance of the common property and the contingency reserve fund, and in some buildings heat, hot water or other services. The Form B Information Certificate lists exactly what a unit's fee covers.
